items.q: A dozen buns cost $24. How much do 3 buns cost?
items.hint: A dozen is 12. Find 1 bun first.

slips.say: 2 is the cost of 1 bun. How much do 3 buns cost?

tpl.q: A dozen buns cost ${t}. How much do {k} buns cost?
tpl.hint: A dozen is 12. Find 1 bun first.

items.q: 3 pens cost $9. Ben has $12. How many pens can Ben buy?
items.hint: Find 1 pen first. How many groups fit?
steps: How many groups of $3 fit in $12?

slips.say: 3 is the number of pens in the story. How many $3 pens can Ben buy with $12?

tpl.q: {n} pens cost ${t}. Ben has ${m}. How many pens can Ben buy?
tpl.hint: Find 1 pen first. How many groups fit?
steps: How many groups of ${u} fit in ${m}?

items.q: 2 hats cost $10. 3 scarves cost $18. Jenny buys 1 hat and 2 scarves. How much does Jenny pay?
items.hint: Find the cost of 1 hat and of 1 scarf first.

slips.say: 28 adds the two totals. Find 1 hat and 1 scarf first.

tpl.q: 2 hats cost ${h}. 3 scarves cost ${s}. Jenny buys 1 hat and 2 scarves. How much does Jenny pay?
tpl.hint: Find the cost of 1 hat and of 1 scarf first.

items.q: 6 pens cost $18. Mei has $20. She buys 4 pens. How much money does Mei have left?
items.hint: Find 1 pen, then 4 pens, then what is left.

items.q: Make your own shop puzzle. Choose a price for 1 pen and a number of pens. Write how much the pens cost in all, and ask a grown-up to find the price of 1 pen. Many answers are right.
items.hint: Start with the price of 1 pen, then multiply.
steps: Write how much they cost in all.
Ask a grown-up to find 1 pen.
